I've been away from MAME for a long time (since the 16 bit days) but recently got interested in it again. I downloaded the latest MAME and discovered that it wouldn't run some of the games that worked just fine in older versions. Those games displayed the "Selected game missing one or more required ROM" error. Many explanations that I found on the web made no sense, since the games that no longer worked had not changed. It was MAME itself that had changed. I think what's going on is that the MAME devs have decided to implement new features in a way that breaks backward compatibility. For example, if emulation of some sound circuitry is added and the sound processor used a ROM, then that ROM is now required by MAME or the game won't run at all. The right thing would've been to allow a ROM subset that worked in a previous version of MAME to work in a new version without the added new circuitry emulation where possible, but that's a fair bit of additional coding and it's understandable why it was done that way. Here's how I figured out what additional files to look for to make an older ROM set work with a newer version of MAME. I'll use "asteroid" as an example. These commands are run from the command line in the directory where MAME is installed.

"mame asteroid -listcrc" showed me individual ROM files and their CRCs that the new version of MAME required
"mame asteroid -listroms" is the same, but also with sizes and SHA hashes
"mame asteroid -verifyroms" told me which individual ROM file were missing from roms\asteroid.zip

Something like "asteroid : xyzzy.bin (1024 bytes) - NOT FOUND" appeared.
At that point, the hunt was on for xyzzy.bin

Once I had accumulated the missing required files, I created a new zip file containing all of them and replaced my old .zip file in the roms directory with it. The -verifyroms check displayed no more "NOT FOUND" messages and I was good to go.
